items.q: What kind of role are you looking for?
items.a: Senior product designer or design lead roles, especially on B2B and enterprise products where the workflow is complicated and the team needs someone to make it clear.

items.q: How much experience do you have?
items.a: 9+ years in product design, across complex SaaS, AI-assisted and enterprise products. Before that I studied at BCIT, where I now teach.

items.q: Where do you work now?
items.a: I'm the Lead Product Designer at MAVI, where I own design across their AI-assisted talent, customer and internal products. I also teach UX/UI in BCIT's D3 program.

items.q: Do you have AI product experience?
items.a: Yes. At MAVI I design AI-assisted hiring and vetting workflows, and at Copperleaf I designed predictive, AI-powered maps and scenario tools. I care about keeping people in control of the automation.

items.q: Do you lead or mentor other designers?
items.a: Yes. I teach at BCIT, mentor through Vancouver Design Community, run portfolio reviews, and have mentored at Pathrise and IterateUX. Several of the recommendations on this site are from people I mentored.
items.tags: mentor lead leadership manage coach teach

items.q: What was the MAVI client portal?
items.a: Clients were running hiring through email and disconnected tools. I led design on one portal to review candidates, book interviews and sign agreements, and got the PM, Platform, Sales, Customer Success and our co-founder aligned in under two weeks.
items.tags: mavi client portal hiring

items.q: What were the key decisions on MAVI?
items.a: Removing a metric that looked helpful but would have created doubt for clients, cutting the main decision screen to two choices, dropping a gated step-by-step flow, and scoping the MVP to review, schedule and sign. The full story is in the locked part of the case study.
items.tags: mavi decisions tradeoffs mvp scope

items.q: What did you do at Copperleaf?
items.a: I made Framework Designer, a complex enterprise tool, easier to learn. 23 interviews and test sessions, 23 ideas narrowed to three tested directions, then a resource guide shipped in the product and an assistant prototyped in Pendo.
items.tags: copperleaf framework designer enterprise

items.q: What were the results at Copperleaf?
items.a: A resource map shipped inside the product, a first version of a guided assistant tried through Pendo with no developer time, which saved an estimated 3 months of build, and a usability baseline (SUS 64.7) for measuring future changes.
items.tags: copperleaf results outcomes impact metrics numbers

items.q: What was UI Avenue?
items.a: A startup app that made Google Analytics readable for shop owners. I was the founding product designer from 2019. It launched, and the company closed a few months later at the start of the pandemic.
items.tags: ui avenue startup analytics google
